title: Subject-To & Wraparound Note Arbitrage — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Field worksheets for wrap mechanics, subject-to acquisition, wrap arbitrage, seller-finance terms, hybrid structuring, and due-on-sale defense, built from operator numbers and closing-table rules

worksheets.title: Wrap Mechanics and the Subject-To Acquisition File
worksheets.purpose: Document the underlying loan, the wrap structure that rides on it, and the seller pitch that puts the deal under contract, so the spread is earned on the full balance and every payment, recording, and called-loan decision is written down before closing.
instructions: Pull every underlying loan figure from the lender itself, using an authorization to release, before entering any number in this worksheet.
Work the spread math on the full balance, comparing a separate second lien against an all-inclusive wrap on the same numbers.
Write the payment waterfall so a servicer pays the underlying lender first and the wrap holder last, every single month.
Name the called-loan plan with a refinance path, reserves, and a dated timeline before signing any purchase agreement.
Treat disclosure as the core of the business: explain the existing mortgage and the due-on-sale clause to the buyer in writing, up front and again at closing.

fields.name: underlying_loan_profile
fields.prompt: Record the live underlying loan you intend to wrap or take subject-to: lender, current principal balance, note rate, monthly payment, remaining term, and whether the note carries a due-on-sale clause. State how you verified each figure directly with the lender.
fields.example: Virginia Beach 3bd/1ba preforeclosure: $119,000 principal, $1,100 PITI, ARV $230,000 to $240,000. A bankruptcy discharge made every missed payment due, so the reinstatement came to $46,000 and roughly $50,000 to get in, confirmed with an authorization to release form signed by the seller [kris haskins — DhOoZcypJCM @ 00:07:25]. Lender figures only, no seller estimates.

fields.name: spread_on_full_balance
fields.prompt: Compare the income from carrying a separate second lien against an all-inclusive wrap on the same deal. Show the rate earned on the equity portion and the rate gap earned on the underlying balance, and explain which structure you will use.
fields.example: Underlying $80,000 at 4%. A $20,000 second at 6% earns 6% only on the second. An all-inclusive wrap for $100,000 at 6% earns 6% on the $20,000 equity plus the 2% difference on the first $80,000 [kris haskins — kM__5b36grI @ 00:10:56]. Decision: write the all-inclusive wrap so the spread runs on the full balance.

fields.name: full_cycle_profit_model
fields.prompt: Model the full-cycle profit of your wrap: down payment collected, monthly spread multiplied across the balloon term, and the gap between the wrap balance and the underlying balance at payoff. Total all three and state the balloon length you assumed.
fields.example: $300,000 underlying at 3.5% wrapped into a $350,000 sale at 5% with $10,000 down. Monthly spread $531.75 over a 10-year balloon equals $63,810 cash flow; balance gap at payoff $52,415.31. Total about $126,000 [Chris Goff — X_UODDIMvFs @ 00:05:32]. Every component traces to the amortization schedule, not a rounded guess, and the balloon date is written into the note.

fields.name: mirror_vs_equity_wrap
fields.prompt: Decide whether you are buying on a mirror wrap or selling on an equity wrap, or both. Record the equity position, the price markup, and the interest rate markup that turns a thin-equity acquisition into a full-balance spread on resale.
fields.example: Little or no equity on entry, so buy on a mirror wrap, then sell on an equity wrap that marks up both price and rate [kris haskins — kM__5b36grI @ 00:13:02]. High-end check: a $2,400 all-inclusive payment that rents for only $2,500 fails as a rental, but an owner-carry wrap with a raised rate catches $400 to $600 monthly.

fields.name: acquisition_stance
fields.prompt: State your acquisition stance on wraps. Note where respected operators disagree about buying on a wrap versus selling on one, which side you are taking on this deal, and what structure you will use instead if you refuse to buy on a wrap.
fields.example: Pace Morby: never buy on a wrap, sell on a wrap [Pace Morby — hTxjhDN2Cyo @ 00:05:25]; he prefers split-note hybrids on the acquisition. Brian Gibbons issues a different warning and says never sell on a seller-held wrap. My stance: acquire subject-to with a separate seller note, then dispose on a wrap routed through a third-party servicer.

fields.name: security_instrument_and_recording
fields.prompt: Identify exactly what gets recorded at the county and what stays unrecorded. Name the security instrument, the wraparound rider attached to it, and who holds the original note, so nobody mistakes a notarized note for recorded security. Confirm the closer agrees.
fields.example: Recorded: deed of trust with the all-inclusive wraparound rider as the security instrument. Unrecorded: the wrap note, held in the original by the holder. People notarize notes and record them, and those do not mean anything; a mortgage or deed of trust is required [kris haskins — kM__5b36grI @ 00:16:52]. Closer confirmed the rider before signing.

fields.name: servicer_waterfall
fields.prompt: Name the loan servicer who will collect every buyer payment, and write out the payment order: who gets paid first, who gets paid last, and how you will receive proof that the underlying lender was paid each month without relying on the seller.
fields.example: Buyer pays the servicer; the servicer pays the mortgage company first and pays the wrap holder whatever is left over, which the industry calls its fraud preventer [Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network — VDXOvtqzbZk @ 00:07:47]. Just paying the seller and hoping the seller pays carries real risk, and an escrow company speeds the process.

fields.name: due_on_sale_plan
fields.prompt: Write the exact plan you will execute if the underlying lender calls the loan due. Include the refinance path, the reserves set aside, and the timeline, and confirm whether the loan is assumable or carries a due-on-sale clause before you sign anything.
fields.example: Called-loan plan named in advance: refinance path, cash reserves, and a dated timeline [Tim Talks Real Estate — Dklhw3jMfVo @ 00:05:31]. Loan carries a due-on-sale clause; the textbook case warns there is a lot of risk unless the loan is assumable with no such clause. Disclosure handled up front, since 90% of the wrap business is proper disclosure.

fields.name: lender_access_package
fields.prompt: List the documents you collected to speak with the seller's mortgage company before closing, and record the arrears, reinstatement, and payoff figures you obtained. Note whether escrow is open and whether the title report is in hand, and list any issues it shows.
fields.example: Lender access package assembled first: the seller's SSN, an authorization to release, and a notarized limited POA [kris haskins — FybFcuS9T7s @ 00:06:23]. No move-out date promised until escrow opened and the title report arrived, because Morby says 99% of the reports he sees show issues. Opening escrow is where the challenges actually start.

fields.name: seller_pitch_and_entry_fee
fields.prompt: Script your seller pitch and score your entry fee. Show the seller's retail-sale cost, your cash offer anchor, the takeover terms you will offer, and every dollar of cash needed to get in as a percentage of value, scored against a 25% ceiling.
fields.example: Owes $160,000, comps $260,000. Entry: $8,000 commission, $4,000 TC plus closing, $15,000 wholesale fee, $5,000 to the seller, so $32,000 out of $192,000 scores 16%, under the 25% ceiling [Flipping Mastery TV — rYMNGajRMfo @ 00:02:27]. Pitch: a retail listing costs about 10% in commissions and closing costs; taking over payments hands the seller a small check instead.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when all ten fields hold lender-verified figures, the security instrument and wraparound rider are identified for recording, a servicer is named to pay the underlying lender first, the called-loan plan lists refinance path, reserves, and timeline, and the entry fee scores under the 25% ceiling.

worksheets.title: Wrap Arbitrage and Seller-Finance Terms Sheet
worksheets.purpose: Price the resale wrap for spread, down payment, and cash flow, then negotiate seller-finance terms on price, down payment, rate, and length, so both sides of the deal are underwritten against rent, buyer affordability, and the payment path to the underlying lender.
instructions: Structure the monthly payment first and rent-test it against local market rent before setting the wrap price or note rate.
Vet every non-qualifying buyer for affordability of the full payment, not just the down payment, before selling to them.
Use plain seller language: describe seller financing with the existing loan staying in place and principal only payments.
Negotiate all four terms together, conceding price only when the seller gives terms in exchange.
Fund a 12-month escrow prepay for taxes and insurance from the buyer's down payment and route lender payments so the seller is never a pass-through.

fields.name: sub_to_wrap_entry_profit
fields.prompt: Compare the buyer's down payment on your wrap against your own cash in on the subject-to acquisition. Record the underlying rate, your all-in basis, the wrap price, the wrap note amount and rate, and the entry profit before cash flow.
fields.example: Tampa sub-to at 2.75%, $330,000 all-in, $40,000 of operator cash. Resold on a $400,000 wrap with a $350,000 note at 7% and a $50,000 down payment, so $10,000 is made before the house starts cash flowing [Dom Inglese — Lv34MZLHg1I @ 00:03:24]. Monthly spread is upside on top of an entry that already paid.

fields.name: total_collections_projection
fields.prompt: Project total collections over the full life of the wrap note: sale price, down payment, note amount, rate, and amortization. Then discount the total for time value of money and compare it against the equity you actually gave up.
fields.example: $100,000 sale, $10,000 down, $90,000 at 9.5% over 30 years: $142,377 of total collections on $20,000 of equity, discounted a third to a half for time value of money [Propelio TV — pCK7ihJF_-Q @ 00:16:10]. A higher underlying rate still works: a $64,000 underlying at 9.5% costs $539 while a $90,000 wrap at 9% brings $724.

fields.name: buyer_payment_vs_rent
fields.prompt: Set the wrap payment by structuring the monthly number first, then rent-test it. Record the local market rent, the proposed monthly payment, the note rate you will not lead with, and whether the payment would sit unsold at that level.
fields.example: Talk about the monthly payment, not the interest rate, and benchmark it against local rent; 9% is possible [Caleb Christopher — UOyoE5Fc7VE @ 00:02:24]. Fail case: wraps priced at $6,000 a month in $3,500 rent areas sit unsold. Pass case: Nick Disney's typical $150,000 note at 10.9%, about $1,400 monthly over 30 years.

fields.name: buyer_affordability_vetting
fields.prompt: Describe how you vetted the non-qualifying buyer for affordability of the full payment before selling the property. Identify the buyer profile, the income documentation you reviewed, and why a bank turned this buyer down. Note any red flags that remain open.
fields.example: Buyer is a penalty box buyer: ITIN holder with a cash job, not bankable [Dom Inglese — StKrDLiCONM @ 00:04:00]. Affordability vetted against the full wrap payment, not just the down payment, before any sale. Down payment funds a 12-month escrow prepay for taxes and insurance at closing, so the first year of escrow cannot lapse.

fields.name: seller_language
fields.prompt: Write the exact words you will use with the seller to describe the structure. Avoid jargon that confuses, record the phrase you will use for the existing loan staying in place, and note how you describe the payments.
fields.example: Never say wrap or subject-to; call it seller financing where the existing loan stays in place, because a confused mind says no [Creative Finance Playbook — u3lV-kVx-LU @ 00:02:36]. On free-and-clear deals, write principal only payments, never zero percent, in every written offer and on every seller call, exactly as Pace Morby teaches.

fields.name: four_terms_negotiation
fields.prompt: Lay out the four negotiable terms on a seller-finance deal: price, down payment, interest rate, and length. Show what the seller asked for, what you offered in exchange, and how paying the seller's number bought you better terms.
fields.example: Susan, I would be willing to come up to your number if you would be willing to give me terms [Pace Morby — 6FXApQ1y2KE @ 00:06:35]. Result: mobile home closed at $110K, principal-only, $10K down split into two $5K installments, $375 a month, against a best cash offer of $57K. Price conceded; terms won.

fields.name: note_rate_and_balloon
fields.prompt: Choose the rate and balloon on the seller note and defend both. Compare a principal-only note against a 6 to 9 percent note with a 5 to 7 year balloon, and record your extension clause or refinance plan.
fields.example: Key & Capital models 6-9% rates with 5-7 year balloons and refuses any balloon shorter than 12 months and builds in an extension clause, refinance plan, or fully amortizing note [Key & Capital — dzuLMB2Szxc @ 00:10:38]. Pace counters that a high note rate tells the buyer to refinance the seller out fast, while 0% locks the price.

fields.name: bank_vs_seller_payment
fields.prompt: Run the bank-versus-seller payment comparison on the same property. Record the financed amount, the bank rate and payment, the seller rate and payment, the monthly savings, and the total savings over your expected hold period. Note the cash a bank requires down.
fields.example: $300K Dallas duplex, 20% down, $240K financed on a 30-year amortization: bank at 7.32% runs $1,649 a month, seller at 6% runs $1,439, saving $210 monthly, $2,520 yearly, and $12,600 over 5 years [Key & Capital — dzuLMB2Szxc @ 00:04:24]. A bank wants 30-35% down; Pace's average all-in entry is about 8%.

fields.name: assignment_fee_and_cash_on_cash
fields.prompt: Price the assignment fee and the expected return. Record net monthly cash flow after the seller payment, taxes, insurance, and reserves, apply the per-hundred-dollar fee rule, and confirm the deal clears your cash-on-cash target minimum before signing.
fields.example: Rule of thumb: $2,000 of assignment fee per $100 of net monthly cash flow, or $5,000 per $100 at 0% interest [Flipping Mastery TV — MeNrueZIYeE @ 00:24:45]. A deal netting $500 a month supports a $10K fee. Target 30%+ cash-on-cash, and never be the party that writes the first check.

fields.name: servicing_and_payment_control
fields.prompt: Decide how the underlying lender gets paid on your wrap and who controls that flow. Choose between a servicer, a clearing house that sends receipts, or direct payment, and confirm the seller never acts as a pass-through.
fields.example: Never let the seller act as a pass-through; pay the original lender directly or through a clearing house that sends receipts [Caleb Christopher — UBngwrCrCxM @ 00:05:36]. Horne Real Estate Law always uses a servicer, reporting due-on-sale in 13 cases out of 10,000 deals, while Nick Disney pays lenders directly. Chosen path: servicer with monthly receipts.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when the wrap payment passes a local rent test, the buyer affordability file covers the full payment, the seller note has a rate and balloon with an extension or refinance plan, the payment path to the underlying lender bypasses the seller, and the 12-month escrow prepay is funded at closing.

worksheets.title: Hybrid Structuring and Due-on-Sale Defense Plan
worksheets.purpose: Layer the subject-to loan, the seller equity note, and any private money into one hybrid, then document the timing, insurance, entity, and cure steps that keep the due-on-sale clause from turning a rare call into a lost property.
instructions: Map each layer of the hybrid separately, with balance, rate, payment, and balloon, before combining them into one entry fee.
Get real payoff and arrears figures from the lender and add about $5,000 for legal fees the title company will miss.
Total every underlying lien, including modification and HUD liens, and keep the wrap balance at or above that total.
Hold the deed transfer until 10 to 15 days after any reinstatement and lock the insurance structure at closing.
Write the acceleration cure before closing: 30-day payoff source, deed-back fallback, and a rule that nothing false ever reaches the lender.

fields.name: hybrid_structure
fields.prompt: Map the hybrid: the existing loan you are taking subject-to, the seller equity carried on a separate note, and any private money in third position funding the entry fee. Record balance, rate, payment, and balloon for each layer.
fields.example: Colorado Springs townhouse: 2.99% loan stays in place subject-to; sellers knocked 20k off the equity in exchange for 1.5% so they could sell the note, finishing at 146,000, $400 a month, 10-year balloon [James Heller -- Hellerman Industries — nO_A1GtSlaA @ 00:05:26]. Private money sits in third position only if the entry fee requires it.

fields.name: acquire_hybrid_dispo_wrap
fields.prompt: Show the arbitrage when you acquire on a hybrid and dispose on a wrap. Record the underlying rate kept clean on acquisition, the wrap rate charged to your end buyer, and the spread you capture between them.
fields.example: Do not buy on a wrap; keep the sub-to note clean, acquire on hybrid and dispo on wrap, where a 6% wrap over a 3% loan is the arbitrage [Flipping Mastery TV — 6Bdxz-HKeFI @ 00:05:33]. Hybrids are about 15% of Pace's creative acquisitions. Landlord Dropout's warning applies: if the buyer stops paying, the underlying payment still remains.

fields.name: no_money_down_cash_flow
fields.prompt: Build the net monthly cash flow on a no-money-down seller-finance rental. Start with market rent, subtract the seller payment, taxes and insurance, and a vacancy and repair reserve, then record the note balance and term. Confirm the result is positive.
fields.example: $1,650 rent minus a $375 seller payment, $150 taxes and insurance, and a $200 vacancy and repair reserve nets $925 a month on a $100k 0% note paid over 240 months [Pace Morby — Ke0nzzYXEfk @ 00:02:38]. About 70% of Pace's deals still need private money for the entry fee; the rest close without it.

fields.name: arrears_and_payoff_verification
fields.prompt: Record the payoff and arrears figures exactly as the lender stated them, not as the title company estimated them. Add your legal-fee cushion, and show how the corrected number changes the entry fee you are funding at closing.
fields.example: The title company is not the bank, so expect the arrears to be off by about $5,000 in legal fees [Pace Morby — t7aFESM6V_k @ 00:05:54]. Real payoff and arrears pulled from the lender, then $5,000 added to the entry fee budget. Private lender in third position sized to the corrected figure, not the title estimate.

fields.name: wrap_balance_vs_liens
fields.prompt: List every lien under the wrap, including modification liens, down-payment assistance, and zero-payment HUD liens. Total them and confirm the wrap balance is at least equal to all underlying debt so the position cannot drift upside down.
fields.example: The wrap balance has to be at least equal to all of the underlying debt [Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network — it6vSh38OhY @ 00:04:30]. Lien schedule: first mortgage, modification lien, down-payment assistance, and a 0% no-payment HUD lien, all totaled against the wrap balance. Borrower pre-screened in five minutes for bankruptcies, foreclosures, and missed payments in 12 months.

fields.name: morby_method_gate
fields.prompt: Decide whether a Morby Method structure fits this deal. Record why the seller's cash-down demand could not be negotiated away, the seller's ownership share in your buyer LLC, and the active income the property already produces.
fields.example: Hard fast rule: if there is not active income coming in on the deal, no Morby Method [Pace Morby — rQCg4GFRLAI @ 00:05:44], because people take the cash out and bail on the payments. The method swaps seller carryback for seller ownership in the buyer LLC. Vacant property here, so the structure is killed and renegotiated.

fields.name: reinstatement_timing
fields.prompt: If the loan was in foreclosure, record the reinstatement date, the planned escrow closing date, and the days between them. Note how long you will hold the physical warranty deed when the loan sits with a small local bank.
fields.example: Catch up the payments, then wait about 10 to 15 days after the loan is reinstated to close escrow [Pace Morby — cOTyo3LTDPk @ 00:03:27]. Transferring the deed 3 days into reinstatement is Morby's most common cause of a call. Small-bank loan, so the physical warranty deed is held about 30 days before recording.

fields.name: insurance_structure
fields.prompt: Write out the insurance structure on the property: who is the named insured, who is additional insured, and who is listed as mortgagee. On a wrap, record the end buyer's policy and your position as secondary mortgagee.
fields.example: Investor named insured, seller additional insured, lender as mortgagee; on the wrap, the end buyer is named insured with the investor as secondary mortgagee [Investor Army Podcast — WFGzQCgPP54 @ 00:04:00]. Botched insurance is a real trigger for a due-on-sale call, alongside missed payments, bad paperwork, and angry sellers or ex-spouses on the loan.

fields.name: llc_trust_transfer
fields.prompt: If title moves into an LLC or land trust, record the entity, its ownership percentages, and how they match the deed. Note the loan investor and origination date, and how you will answer any lender letter asking to verify ownership.
fields.example: Fannie Mae exempts transfers to a borrower-controlled LLC on loans from June 1st, 2016 onward; Freddie Mac requires the original borrower as managing member [Ken McElroy — ulx_sqYnYVA @ 00:04:01]. Verification letters get answered with the operating agreement or land trust agreement, never ignored. Morby's caution stands: a land trust does not stop the clause.

fields.name: called_loan_cure
fields.prompt: Write the cure sequence for an acceleration letter. Record the cure window, the cash or refinance source to pay the balance, the deed-back fallback, and confirm that nothing false will ever be sent to the lender.
fields.example: Every clause reviewed across private, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, FHA, and VA loans gives 30 days to pay the full balance, and lenders usually also offer a 30-day title-back option [In Rem Podcast — d9fjKwIC-VE @ 00:00:41]. Fallback: deed back plus an agreement for sale. A false affidavit emailed to a lender is wire fraud and bank fraud.

worksheets.completion_gate: Complete only when every hybrid layer is mapped, arrears carry the legal-fee cushion, the wrap balance covers all underlying liens, reinstatement timing and insurance roles are recorded, any Morby Method structure shows active income, and the called-loan cure names a funding source and a deed-back fallback.

worksheets.title: Failure-Mode Defense and Creative Closing Control
worksheets.purpose: Stress-test a subject-to or wrap file against the ways these deals go sideways: seller bankruptcy clawbacks, insurance trip switches, misdirected closing packets, and called notes. Then lock down the closing table, Texas disclosure timing, and year-one installment-sale tax so the deal survives title, the lender, and Form 6252.
instructions: Complete every field before scheduling closing, because the failure modes captured here are cheapest to prevent at the table and most expensive to repair after the deed records.
Interview the seller directly about bankruptcy, judgments, liens, and insurance, and attach the title search, declarations page, and signed affidavits to the deal folder for each answer.
Write the called-note plan B as a dated sequence of actions with named funding sources, not as a general intention, so it can be executed inside a roughly 30-day window.
Vet the title company or law-firm closing office in writing, including its named closer, underwriter requirements, draft settlement statement, and wiring policy, before sending the file.
Run the installment-sale tax model with real numbers for contract price, gross profit, payments, and recapture, and revise the down payment if the year-one tax exceeds the cash received.

fields.name: seller_bankruptcy_screen
fields.prompt: Record the seller's bankruptcy status and solvency screen before closing. Note whether you asked point-blank about a current or planned filing, what judgments, tax liens, collections, or pending evictions surfaced, and which reaffirmation clause and notarized solvency affidavit you attached.
fields.example: Asked the seller point-blank whether they were in or considering bankruptcy and got a clear no. The title search showed one paid collection, no judgments, no tax liens and no pending evictions, so the file moved forward with a reaffirmation clause and a notarized affidavit of solvency signed at the table [William Tingle — D8NZHrMYpSE @ 00:06:02].

fields.name: insurance_trigger_lock
fields.prompt: Document the insurance structure locked at closing. State whether the seller switched to a landlord policy, who is named insured and additional insured, who is mortgagee, and how you kept the seller relationship clean enough to call on later.
fields.example: Seller converted the owner-occupant homeowner's policy to a landlord policy the day of closing, with the investor added as additional insured and the original lender kept as mortgagee. Since the declarations page is the trigger roughly 90% of the time, the change was made early and the seller agreed to help with renewals [James Bealer — Y7CyY8gLd3U @ 00:03:10].

fields.name: due_on_sale_plan_b
fields.prompt: Write the plan B if the underlying lender calls the note. Name the payoff source, the refinance path, the deed-back and restructure option, the reserve amount, and the day-by-day timeline that fits inside the roughly 30-day window after a notice.
fields.example: If PennyMac or any servicer calls the loan while payments are current, the first move mirrors Evan Ragsdale's cure: deed the property back to the original borrower, then restructure as a contract for deed on the same economics, keeping control, cash flow and upside. Refinance quotes stay on file as the backup [Evan Ragsdale — m8scT0nPuzY @ 00:02:08].

fields.name: closing_packet_routing
fields.prompt: Track where the executed closing packet travels after signing. List the deed, settlement statement, trust documents and title exception sheet, the only approved recipient, the carrier tracking number, and who confirmed delivery so nothing lands on the lender's desk.
fields.example: Mobile notary instructed in writing to ship the signed packet only to the title company, never to the mortgage servicer. A misdirected FedEx once put the deed and trust documents on Freedom Mortgage's desk, so this file logs the tracking number and a same-day delivery confirmation from the escrow officer [Sub2Investor — WxPHAXmQ-j4 @ 00:05:08].

fields.name: title_company_vetting
fields.prompt: Score the title company or law-firm closing office before sending the file. Record the named closer, its underwriter requirements, whether the draft settlement statement avoids showing the existing loan as a payoff, and its policy on emailed wiring instruction changes.
fields.example: Called three offices. The winner named one closer, stated its underwriter requirements for a subject-to file, and sent a draft settlement statement that kept the existing loan in place rather than listing it as a payoff. It also confirmed it never changes wiring instructions by email and expects callbacks to a known number [Music City TC — -AAdJ4WwUuM @ 00:03:25].

fields.name: texas_disclosure_timing
fields.prompt: If the property sits in Texas, log the date the buyer received the written list of every existing loan with due-on-sale and insurance warnings, the closing date, and the day count proving at least seven days passed between them.
fields.example: Texas wrap: the buyer signed receipt of the underlying-lien notice ten days before the scheduled closing, listing the first lien and a small second, each with due-on-sale and insurance-risk warnings. Ten days clears the seven-day minimum, so the buyer cannot cancel and recover earnest money for late notice [Attorney Hamilton Rucker — 4coBBRVrtIA @ 00:05:06].

fields.name: dual_insurance_policies
fields.prompt: On a wrap sale, describe both insurance policies in force. Identify the seller's original policy kept alive for the old bank, the separate buyer policy, the named insureds and mortgagees on each, and who monitors renewal and cancellation notices.
fields.example: The seller wanted to cancel the old policy to save money, which is the mistake that makes the old bank see its required coverage lapse and move toward foreclosure. The original policy stays in force for the underlying lender, and the end buyer binds a separate policy naming the investor as secondary mortgagee [Attorney Hamilton Rucker — 4coBBRVrtIA @ 00:04:32].

fields.name: wrap_spread_check
fields.prompt: Enter the underlying loan rate, the wrap note rate, and the resulting interest spread. Explain why the spread is wide enough to cover servicing, insurance gaps, and a possible six-month foreclosure stretch if the wrap buyer stops paying.
fields.example: Underlying loan at 3.5%, wrap carried at 6%, a 2.5-point spread on the full wrapped balance. Attorney Patrick McQueen frames 5.5% to 6% as the range where a seller holding a 3.5% loan earns on the rate difference, and the margin here also funds reserves for missed buyer payments [KELLY ZITLOW — pYujIjfIOkE @ 00:05:59].

fields.name: installment_sale_tax_model
fields.prompt: Model year-one tax before signing. Show the contract price, gross profit, gross profit percentage, year-one payments received, taxable gain, any depreciation recapture taxed in full, and any mortgage above basis treated as a payment in the sale year.
fields.example: Rental building sold for $1,200,000 with $240,000 down and a $960,000 note at 6.5%. Gross profit of $728,000 over the contract price gives a 0.6067 gross profit percentage. Year-one payments of $250,730 times that percentage produce $152,118 of taxable gain before recapture is added and checked against cash in hand [Hans Goldstein: Tax & Exit Planning — mIvRRP_DEd0 @ 00:01:46].

fields.name: dealer_down_payment_cushion
fields.prompt: If you are a dealer or flipper barred from installment treatment, calculate the down payment needed to cover the full tax on the gain at closing, and state how later payments will be taxed only on interest.
fields.example: As a flipper, installment treatment is off the table, so the down payment was backed into from the tax bill rather than from the buyer's comfort. The buyer brings enough cash at closing to cover the full tax on the overall gain, leaving every later note payment as after-tax money taxed only on interest [Mark J Kohler — jThMHTcyEdY @ 00:01:40].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not close until the seller has denied any bankruptcy plan in writing, the landlord policy and buyer policy are bound with correct insureds and mortgagees, the packet recipient is locked to the title company, Texas notice timing is proven where applicable, and the year-one tax model shows cash received covering the tax due.

worksheets.title: Dodd-Frank Coverage, Ability-to-Repay, and Servicing Back Office
worksheets.purpose: Decide whether an owner-carry sale falls under Dodd-Frank, document the eight ability-to-repay factors with a licensed originator, and board the note with a licensed servicer whose fee schedule, payment waterfall, document audit, and payoff verification make the paper compliant, collectible, and sellable.
instructions: Start with occupancy: identify who will actually live in the property before choosing an exemption lane, because the name on the deed never decides coverage.
Engage a licensed mortgage loan originator for any file that cannot clearly use an exemption, and keep the originator's work product in the permanent loan file.
Calculate debt-to-income and residual income from documented figures, and decline any buyer who passes the ratio but cannot carry the full payment month to month.
Compare at least two servicers by laying each fee schedule over its servicing agreement, then confirm the payment waterfall pays the underlying lien before anyone else.
Audit the note, notary block, and recording proof before boarding, and obtain every payoff figure directly from the lender or that lender's own servicer.

fields.name: occupancy_coverage_test
fields.prompt: Determine whether Dodd-Frank applies by recording the buyer's true intended occupancy, not the name on the deed. Note whether a buyer LLC, relative, or investor story is involved, and whether a signed business-purpose acknowledgment limits residence to fourteen days yearly.
fields.example: Buyer asked to close in an LLC and described the house as an investment, but a follow-up call revealed the buyer's sister would live there full time. Occupancy purpose decides coverage, so the file was treated as a primary-residence owner-carry loan and routed for a full ability-to-repay review [William Bronchick — ZGvGq-_10yA @ 00:37:21].

fields.name: exemption_lane
fields.prompt: Identify which exemption lane, if any, this sale uses. State whether the seller is a natural person, estate, or trust using the one-property pass, or counts toward three deals in twelve months, and confirm balloon and adjustment-cap limits.
fields.example: Seller is an individual carrying a second deal this year, so the three-property lane applies. The note runs fixed for at least five years, has no negative amortization, caps adjustments at 2% per year and 6% lifetime, and carries no balloon. Outside Texas, processing the buyer on the first deal is still standard [Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network — 1WQyfpf7efQ @ 00:02:17].

fields.name: originator_engagement
fields.prompt: Record the licensed mortgage loan originator engaged for this file, the fee and who pays it, the time required, and which tasks they completed, including the application, documentation of the eight factors, and the printed disclosure stack.
fields.example: Engaged an originator down the hall for $500 and roughly 40 minutes of work. The originator took the buyer's application, documented all eight ability-to-repay factors, and printed the full disclosure stack for signing. Even where an originator is optional, using one kills the borrower's later excuse and protects the seller [William Bronchick — ZGvGq-_10yA @ 00:32:42].

fields.name: dti_and_residual
fields.prompt: Calculate the buyer's back-end debt-to-income ratio and monthly residual income after the full wrap payment. Compare the ratio to the 43% line and your personal screen, then explain whether family size or living costs make the file fail anyway.
fields.example: Back-end DTI came in at 41%, under the 43% line yet well above the three-to-one personal screen of about 33%. With four children in California and only about $500 left each month, the buyer passes the ratio and still fails residual income, so the file is declined [Sub2Investor — 1oenw8zc-5s @ 00:24:46].

fields.name: eight_factor_file
fields.prompt: List the evidence stored for each of the eight ability-to-repay factors, where the written file lives, and the retention date at least three years after consummation, so documented diligence survives a counterclaim or foreclosure defense raised years later.
fields.example: Pay stubs, bank statements, credit report, debt list, and a written DTI and residual worksheet sit in one labeled folder per factor, copied to the servicer. Considering the factors without documentation does not hold up, and borrowers can raise the failure as a foreclosure defense for the life of the loan [William Bronchick — MNznbFmtOwI @ 00:18:16].

fields.name: thin_credit_conditions
fields.prompt: For ITIN, cash-income, or blank-credit buyers, list the income documentation accepted and the conditions requiring twelve months of recurring monthly bills paid, such as utilities, phone, rent, or subscriptions, that establish payment behavior before final approval.
fields.example: Penalty box buyer with an ITIN and documented cash-job income. Approval was conditioned on twelve months of proof that utilities, a phone plan, rent and two online subscriptions were paid every month. Those receipts establish payment behavior that a blank credit report cannot show and go into the underwriting file [Sub2Investor — 1oenw8zc-5s @ 00:21:46].

fields.name: servicer_selection
fields.prompt: Name the licensed servicer boarding this note and the model chosen, full-service or client-managed. Record the quoted monthly fee, the fee schedule laid line by line over the servicing agreement, and any add-on charges discovered before signing.
fields.example: Client-managed servicer quoted $25 per loan per month. Laying the servicer's full fee schedule over the servicing agreement line by line revealed monthly add-ons that pushed the true cost toward $40 to $45, so the quote was renegotiated toward the $30 standard before the note was boarded [7e Investments — SZhJFIusBp4 @ 00:03:22].

fields.name: payment_waterfall
fields.prompt: Map the servicer's payment waterfall for every buyer payment. Record the check-clearing hold, the underlying lien paid first, escrow moved into trust, the servicing fee deducted, and the remainder forwarded to the investor, with receipts sent.
fields.example: Buyer pays by check; the servicer holds it four days to clear, then pays the underlying lien holder, moves the tax and insurance escrow into a trust account, deducts its fee, and forwards the remainder to the investor. The seller is never a pass-through, which is why servicers call this the fraud preventer [Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network — adTW0EyLeRk @ 00:09:56].

fields.name: note_document_audit
fields.prompt: Audit the note package before boarding or buying. Check note length, the notary block, recording proof for the security instrument, and every material term, then decide whether a borrower-signed addendum fixes gaps or a full reclose is required.
fields.example: Promissory note ran four pages, notary block completed, and the deed of trust recorded with the county. One material term was missing, so the borrower signed an addendum rather than redoing the documents, since only an incorrect interest rate or P&I amount forces a full redo of the package [Note Investing & Seller Financing - JKP Holdings — uKK5_EVlvus @ 00:09:09].

fields.name: payoff_verification
fields.prompt: Record how the underlying lien payoff and arrears figures were obtained. Name the lender or its servicer contacted directly, the date, the amount quoted, and the confirmation method, rejecting any figure relayed through a third party.
fields.example: A third party emailed a payoff letter with new wiring details, and it was set aside. The payoff was requested directly from the underlying lender's servicer, confirmed by callback to the number on the original loan statement, and matched to the servicing ledger, because payoff fraud happens out there every day [Scott Horne's Owner Finance Network — adTW0EyLeRk @ 00:16:51].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not fund or board the note until true occupancy is documented, the exemption lane or originator file is complete, DTI and residual income both pass, all eight factors are stored for at least three years, the servicer fee schedule matches the agreement, and every payoff figure came directly from the lender.

worksheets.title: Note Acquisition, Resolution, and Liquidity Exits
worksheets.purpose: Source and price discounted or non-performing mortgage notes with disciplined diligence, resolve defaults through the borrower rather than foreclosure, and plan liquidity exits through full sales, partials, and marketplace listings so capital is recovered while the tail of the note stays in your hands.
instructions: Log the sourcing channel and contact for every note, including servicers, foreclosure attorneys, and marketplace auctions, so repeat off-market supply can be tracked and worked again.
Finish diligence on people, property, and paperwork inside the 14 to 21 day window, and kill the bid if any of the three remains open when the window closes.
Price every bid off the lower of unpaid balance or property value, and confirm the deal still pays at partial recovery rather than full reperformance.
Plan the borrower resolution before closing on the note, including rapport steps, intel targets, delegated authority, and the modification rate you are prepared to write.
Model every partial and marketplace exit with all balances and default scenarios written out, and verify vesting, recording, and seasoning before any collateral changes hands.

fields.name: note_sourcing_channel
fields.prompt: List the sourcing channel for this note, such as a loan servicer, foreclosure attorney, marketplace auction, or direct seller. Record the contact, how they learned the portfolio was for sale, and the season the listing surfaced.
fields.example: Lead came from a foreclosure attorney who handles defaults for several note-owning investors and mentioned one was closing a fund. Servicers are a parallel off-market feed because they know which clients are selling portfolios, and the auction watch list gets extra attention from Thanksgiving on every year [Fusion Notes — PXDW2SqUfMA @ 00:01:36].

fields.name: three_ps_diligence
fields.prompt: Track due diligence on the three Ps, people, property, and paperwork, inside the 14 to 21 day window. Record the BPO value, insurance status, current taxes, borrower intel, and the date diligence finished or the bid was killed.
fields.example: Day 9 of a 21-day window: BPO returned, hazard insurance confirmed active on the property, and county taxes current. The borrower's default traced to a life event, a job loss, and rapport calls suggest a path back to paying. Paperwork review is the remaining gate before the bid is locked [Sierra Davis — UimgP_cJydU @ 00:33:40].

fields.name: bid_price_math
fields.prompt: Show the bid math. Record unpaid principal balance, property value, the lower of the two, your price in cents on the dollar, and the recovery you need, confirming the bid still pays if the loan never fully reperforms.
fields.example: UPB of $100,000 against a $140,000 property value, so pricing runs off the $100,000 UPB. Bid set at 55 cents, $55,000, under the 60-cent ceiling so that even a 70-cent recovery still pays. A price that only works at full reperformance gets killed before submission to the seller [FIXnotes | Non-Performing Note Investing — lxjMbDIOEGw @ 00:04:18].

fields.name: legacy_coupon_adjustment
fields.prompt: If the note carries a legacy 3 to 5 percent coupon, explain how your price absorbs a likely borrower reinstatement and a weaker low-coupon resale, and state the modification rate you would write if the borrower needs one.
fields.example: Note carries a 3.75% legacy rate, so the borrower can likely afford to reinstate, which kills most of the upside. The bid was cut to price in a reinstatement and a weaker resale of low-coupon paper, and any new modification written on this loan starts at 9% or higher [FIXnotes | Non-Performing Note Investing — lxjMbDIOEGw @ 00:07:28].

fields.name: resolution_path
fields.prompt: Choose the primary resolution path through the borrower, such as forbearance, modification, or resale, before foreclosure. Record rapport-building steps, intel gathered on the life event behind the default, delegated authority held, and the target modification turnaround.
fields.example: Holding delegated authority from the servicer, the modification was prepped the same day as the borrower call and sent with the servicer's ACH authorization form. The goal is a modified, reperforming loan within about 30 days, built on rapport and intel rather than a rushed foreclosure filing on day one [FIXnotes | Non-Performing Note Investing — 5H6jVWw2QK0 @ 00:02:02].

fields.name: pay_history_read
fields.prompt: Summarize 12 to 24 months of pay history alongside the servicing notes. Flag rolling 30s or rolling 60s, record what the notes reveal about borrower intent, and state the price adjustment those patterns justify on this note.
fields.example: Eighteen months of ledger show rolling 30s with no 60s, so the price was knocked down rather than walked. The servicing notes mattered more: on a comparable file, a four-years-delinquent contract for deed with a $40,000 payoff sold for about $30,000 because the notes showed the borrower would sign a deed in lieu [Paperstac — VkGqESM8fdY @ 00:03:17].

fields.name: partial_sizing
fields.prompt: Size any partial sale to your cash and yield target. Record the monthly payment, number of payments sold, total payments in the block, the price paid, the resulting partial-buyer yield, and the tail you keep after reassignment.
fields.example: From an $86,900 note at 9.5%, the next 96 of 176 payments were sold for $47,615, giving the partial buyer a 13.3% yield. When the block is paid, the note reassigns and the seller is still owed $47,249, preserving the tail while raising cash today for the next acquisition [Paperstac — UwiEQOh84Y4 @ 00:17:14].

fields.name: default_split_model
fields.prompt: Before selling a partial, model how payoff, auction, and REO outcomes split between the partial investor and the tail holder. Record the reassignment balance, entitlement balance, and current UPB, and who receives proceeds in each scenario.
fields.example: An IRA investor paid 55,000 for the next 120 payments on a mobile-home note, earning 10.48%, while the tail is valued at 95,402 at full term. The split sheet shows who is paid first on an early payoff, at auction, or after an REO resale, tracking all three balances [Cal Ewing — LCY-eZOK6gw @ 00:12:50].

fields.name: wrap_note_first_position
fields.prompt: If the note being sold or partialed is a wrap, document the title run, the underlying lien disclosed to the buyer, and how partial proceeds pay that lien off so the paper moves into first position before trading.
fields.example: Wrap note sits over a small underlying first. Title was run, the underlying lien was disclosed in writing to the partial buyer, and the partial proceeds are wired straight to that lien's payoff so the wrap note moves to first position, since partials on wraps can otherwise get sticky [Paperstac — 5bOm5hdSRXc @ 00:07:29].

fields.name: marketplace_listing_check
fields.prompt: Before listing or bidding on a marketplace, verify rate, UPB, origination date, and last pay date, confirm FBO vesting wording, address, and signer with a screenshot, and record whether assignments and deeds are recorded and the seasoning months.
fields.example: Indicative bid locked off verified rate, UPB, origination date and last pay date, with no blanket $20,000 lowball. FBO wording, address and signer were screenshotted before collateral went to the auditor. With 14 months of seasoning, offers should improve over a one-payment note, and every assignment is recorded [Paperstac — MkofIE1Xq0o @ 00:04:12].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not wire purchase funds or sell any partial until diligence on people, property, and paperwork closed inside the window, the bid pays at partial recovery, a licensed servicer is boarded at closing, default splits are modeled for every scenario, and vesting, assignments, and deeds are verified and recorded.
